cases.title: feat(integration): add none for shared scaffolding only
cases.body:
## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? -->

Add `none` as an ordinary registered built-in integration. It returns an empty command-template list, so inherited setup creates no files. Its teardown is manifest-only: it never invokes shared event cleanup for files it did not create. Teams can initialize shared Spec Kit scaffolding without generating agent commands, skills, settings, or native events:

```bash
specify init my-project --integration none
```

The existing lifecycle handles init, install, use, switch, upgrade, and uninstall without changes. `none` has normal installed/default metadata and an empty owned-file manifest; shared `.specify/` infrastructure remains. `SPECKIT_INTEGRATION_DEFAULT=none` selects it through the existing default configuration.

Use `specify integration switch <key>` to replace it. `none` declares `multi_install_safe = True`, so another declared-safe integration can coexist without `--force`, with healthy status:

```bash
specify integration install kiro-cli
specify integration use kiro-cli
```

Partners not declared safe, including Copilot, still require the existing `--force` override and still produce `unsafe-multi-install` status while coinstalled. No name-based collision exception or automatic fallback installation is added.

The cumulative diff is **10 files, +178/-14**. Executable changes remain the adapter and two-line registry wiring. Supporting changes are catalog metadata, focused tests, reference documentation,

expected.rationale: Enables agent-neutral setup and later switching/coexistence; preservation semantics support this workflow but no broad incident is claimed.

cases.title: fix(extensions): reject malformed catalog entries before removal
cases.body:
## Description

`specify extension catalog remove <name>` drops every entry of `.specify/extension-catalogs.yml` that isn't a mapping while it removes `<name>` (the list comprehension in `src/specify_cli/extensions/catalog/command_remove.py`). One bare URL line, such as `- https://example.com/private.json` instead of a `name`/`url` mapping, is enough:

- Removing a name that isn't in the file still prints `✓ Removed catalog '<name>'`, exits 0, and rewrites the file without the malformed entry. The comment and the CRLF line endings go with it.
- Removing the last valid catalog leaves an empty list, so the command deletes the file, including the user's other top-level keys.

#4992 fixed the same thing in `specify preset catalog remove`. This PR does the same for extensions: every entry is checked before anything is removed, and a non-mapping entry exits 1 with `Invalid catalog entry at index N: expected a mapping, got <type>`, the message #4992 uses. The file is left as it was. Valid configs behave as before.

`specify extension catalog list` already refuses such a file: on the config below it exits 1 with `catalog entry at index 1: expected a mapping, got str` from the shared catalog loader. `remove` rewrote the same file instead.

I haven't seen a user report of this. It came up while checking the other catalog commands after #4992.

Repro: `specify init --here --integration codex --ignore-agent-tools`, then this `.specify/extension-catalogs.yml` (CRLF):

```yaml
# Team confi

expected.rationale: Rejects malformed catalog entries before mutation to prevent losing user configuration, explicitly without a prior user report.

cases.title: fix(scripts): write --json output of the Python helpers as ASCII
cases.body:
## Description

With `--script py`, the command templates run the Python helpers with `--json` and read their stdout. On Windows a captured stdout uses the ANSI code page (cp1252 on most Western setups), and `_json_line` / `json.dumps` write with `ensure_ascii=False`. Any character cp1252 can't encode then raises `UnicodeEncodeError`, the script exits 1, and the agent gets no JSON:

- `resolve_template.py constitution-template --json` (`/speckit.constitution`) fails with the stock template, which contains `→`.
- `setup_tasks.py --json` (`/speckit.tasks`) fails with the stock tasks template, which contains emoji.
- `setup_plan.py --json`, `check_prerequisites.py --json` and `setup_tasks.py --json` fail for any feature whose name isn't Latin. Since #4780, `create_new_feature.py` keeps names like `001-Додати-експорт-звітів`, and these scripts print that path.

#3890 and #3892 fixed the same crash in the text output of `check_prerequisites.py` and `setup_tasks.py`: the check marks fall back to `[OK]`/`[FAIL]` when stdout can't encode them. The `--json` paths, which the command templates use, still crash. This PR writes their JSON with `ensure_ascii=True`. With `--json`, non-ASCII characters are now written using JSON Unicode escapes on all systems, including UTF-8 systems. JSON parsers recover exactly the same values, preserving localized names, paths, and template content. This prevents encoding failures on legacy Windows output code pages. Output without `--json` is unchanged.

expected.rationale: Prevents stock and localized agent workflow helpers from crashing on legacy Windows encoding while preserving JSON values.

cases.title: fix(events): preserve dispatcher ownership during cleanup
cases.body:
## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? -->

Fix shared integration cleanup silently deleting a user-owned `.specify/events.py`.
Previously, cleanup deleted the dispatcher whenever no other installed integration
referenced it, even if the integration performing cleanup had never owned it.
This affected incoming event-capable integration setup as well as teardown.

Require ownership evidence from the integration's current or previous manifest
before deleting the last managed dispatcher. Preserve unowned, recovered, and
partially owned files even when forced, retain dispatchers referenced by another
installed integration, and preserve modified managed dispatchers with a warning
unless forced. Consult the prior manifest during empty-event upgrades so genuine
last-consumer cleanup still works with a fresh output manifest.

Thread force through event emission, teardown, and upgrades; document the event
helper/override contract. Add positive and negative ownership coverage using
existing integrations, including public install, switch, and upgrade commands.
This change contains no new integration adapter or CLI guidance changes.

Regression evidence: replaying the original cleanup function from the branch's
base commit in an isolated pytest process made all 10 unowned-dispatcher cases
fail; the corrected implementation passed those same 10 cases. The tests exercise
both incoming installation and outgoing teardown without requiring the `none`
integration.

```text

cases.title: Fix bare collections.abc stream annotations
cases.body:
## Pull Request

Discussion and team-member invitation: pending; no discussion link or invitation has been recorded.

## Description

Bare stream annotations from `typing` are recognized through `get_origin`, but equivalent classes such as `collections.abc.AsyncIterator` have no origin. They fall through to normal response-model construction and can prevent route registration. Some synchronous classes happen to register through Pydantic, but do not receive consistent stream-item metadata.

When an annotation is a bare class, use the class itself as the candidate origin. The existing supported-stream check then resolves an unparameterized stream to `Any`. Parameterized and unrelated return annotations keep their existing path.

Extend the existing bare-stream tests with 12 combinations: `Iterable`, `Iterator`, `Generator`, `AsyncIterable`, `AsyncIterator` and `AsyncGenerator`, each for JSONL and SSE. These exercise real route registration, requests, decoded payloads and generated OpenAPI metadata.

## Validation

- Baseline with final regressions: 12 failures and four passing existing tests.
- Fixed source: 73 tests pass across the six focused streaming modules.
- Ruff 0.16.10 lint, formatting and Git whitespace checks pass.
- Follow-up CI fix: narrow the registered route to `APIRoute` before reading `stream_item_type`. The CI failure reproduces with locked ty 0.0.78 before this change; the affected-file type check and all 73 focused tests pass afterward.
- Validation used Pyt

expected.rationale: Fixes bare standard-library stream annotations preventing route registration and inconsistent stream metadata acrossJSONL/SSE.

cases.title: 🐛 Fix `include_in_schema=False` ignored for fields of `Query`, `Header` and `Cookie` parameter models
cases.body:
## Pull Request

Discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/16587

## Description

Fields of a `Query`, `Header` or `Cookie` parameter model declared with `include_in_schema=False` were still listed in the generated OpenAPI `parameters`, while the same declaration on a top-level parameter correctly hides it.

```python
class Filter(BaseModel):
    visible: str = "ok"
    hidden: str = Query("secret", include_in_schema=False)


@app.get("/items")
def get_items(f: Annotated[Filter, Query()]):
    return f
```

Before: `/items` exposes `visible` and `hidden`. After: only `visible`. The hidden field is still read from the request and validated as before, this only affects the OpenAPI schema (the same behavior as for top-level parameters).

Root cause: `_get_openapi_operation_parameters()` in `fastapi/openapi/utils.py` checks `include_in_schema` on the parent (model) parameter only, and then flattens the model fields without repeating that check for each field. Other per-field attributes (`description`, `deprecated`, `example`, `convert_underscores`) are already read from the flattened field, so this adds the missing `include_in_schema` check next to them. Request handling is untouched.

Note: the fix applies to fields declared as `field: str = Query(..., include_in_schema=False)`. With `Annotated[str, Query(include_in_schema=False)]` inside a Pydantic model, Pydantic merges the metadata into a plain `FieldInfo` (the FastAPI subclass is only preserved for the assig

expected.rationale: Aligns hidden model-field schema behavior with top-level parameters; request reading/validation is explicitly unchanged, not a security access-control fix.
